sections.h2: Which Johnston County office takes my deed?
sections.html:
The Johnston County Register of Deeds works from the ground floor of the courthouse in Smithfield, Suite 209 at 207 E. Johnston Street, near the 2nd and Market Street corner of Courthouse Square. Land records calls go to 919-989-5160.

Doors are open weekdays from 8:00 to 5:00 except on county holidays, and the real estate counter takes walk-ins without an appointment until 4:45 in the afternoon. Vital records run on their own line, 919-989-5161, so an heir who needs a death certificate for an estate sale should dial that number instead.

Recording matters because priority in North Carolina follows the time of registration in the county where the land lies. A deed still sitting in someone's briefcase gives the buyer no protection against a later purchaser or a lien creditor, so the usual plan is to record on the day the buyer funds.

sections.h2: What does the Johnston County Register of Deeds charge for recording?
sections.html:
Johnston County prices a regular deed at a flat $26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 for every page beyond that. A deed of trust or mortgage gets a longer base, running to page 35 for $64.00. The county's schedule page carries an August 30, 2024 update date.

Johnston County recording charges taken from the register's fee schedule page
Document or serviceCharge listed
Deed, easement or similar instrument$26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 a page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 through page 35, then $4.00 a page
Release of a security instrumentNone
Second or later instrument inside one document$10.00 apiece
Document that breaks the formatting rules$25.00
Plat map$21.00 a page
Certified copy of something recorded$5.00 for page one, $2.00 per page after
Plain copy10 cents a page, $1.00 minimum by mail

Mailed packages that need a refund are not refunded at $1.00 or less. Anything larger comes back as a check from county finance.

sections.h2: How much is the excise tax on a Johnston County deed?
sections.html:
The county's schedule states the excise stamp as $2.00 per $1,000 of consideration, restating it as $1.00 per $500. The seller carries that cost, because state law makes the transferor pay the register ahead of recording.

Where the money lands is split down the middle: one half to the county general fund, one half to the Department of Revenue. The stamp sits on a different line than the per-page fee, and the closing company normally lists both in the seller column of the settlement statement.

Ask the office or your closing attorney for the exact stamp amount on your contract price before closing day, since the rate applies to each $500 or part of $500.

sections.h2: Can a Johnston County deed be recorded electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. The register says Johnston County was among the first North Carolina counties to e-record every document type and among the first anywhere to e-record plat maps, and most of what the office receives now arrives electronically.

Five submitters appear on the county's approved list:

  • CSC eRecording
  • EPN
  • Indecomm
  • NTC
  • Simplifile

A recorded document goes back to the submitter within seconds for review. Title companies and closing attorneys typically hold an account with one of these services, so a seller rarely logs in. If you are closing without a lawyer, ask the person handling your closing which service they use and when the file can go out.

The county also hosts an online search. Visitors can look up a grantor or grantee name, a reception number, a date range or a subdivision, and a find-related function pulls documents sharing a legal description.

sections.h2: What pushes a Johnston County recording bill higher?
sections.html:
Three items add to the base charge, and each has its own line on the county schedule.

  • Length. Every page past 15 on a deed adds $4.00.
  • Bundled instruments. A document holding two or more instruments with different legal effect adds $10.00 for each extra one.
  • Format. A document that misses the recording standards in G.S. 161-14(b) picks up $25.00 on top of the recording fee.

Payoff paperwork is the inexpensive part. A satisfaction, trustee's satisfaction or affidavit of satisfaction carries no charge, so clearing an old loan costs nothing at the register. If your lender has not released its lien, ask it to send the satisfaction for recording right after payoff.

sections.h2: What should be ready before a deed goes to the Johnston County register?
sections.html:
Have the deed signed, notarized and complete before it leaves the closing table. The register records instruments and does not draft or repair them.

A short checklist keeps a closing from stalling:

  • Match the grantor names to the way title is now held.
  • Carry over the parcel description from your own deed.
  • Line up the stamp amount for the seller to pay.
  • Ask your lender to record a satisfaction of the old deed of trust.
  • Ask the Johnston County tax office about any unpaid bill, since the property tax lien attaches to a parcel on the January 1 listing date.

The office also runs a free property fraud alert, with sign-up through the county site. Owners who rent out or leave a house empty during a sale may want it, as the office reports property fraud cases on the rise.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Johnston County for a seller?
sections.html:
Johnston County sits east of Raleigh and has grown fast. The Census Bureau estimates 256,448 residents for July 1, 2025, against a 2020 census count of 215,999, an 18.7 percent rise from the 2020 estimates base. Housing units total 99,408.

In the 2020 to 2024 estimates, the typical owner-occupied home is valued at $305,600, and owners live in 76.1 percent of homes. Households earn a median $83,384 and spend a mean 32.2 minutes getting to work. Gross rent has a median of $1,146, which gives a landlord a rent figure to weigh against an offer.

Construction is brisk, with 3,002 permits recorded for 2025. New houses compete with resales, so buyers on older homes often press for repairs or credits. The county covers 792.02 square miles, a mix of town lots and rural acreage.

sections.h2: What if the house is inherited or has liens in Johnston County?
sections.html:
Start by getting the right paperwork on file. Probate filings go through the clerk of superior court, and the register then records the deeds that follow. North Carolina lets an heir, creditor or public administrator collect by affidavit when personal property less liens is at most $20,000, filed with the clerk in the county of the decedent's domicile.

On liens, the register keeps the index but removes nothing on its own. A mortgage or deed of trust leaves the record only when a satisfaction is recorded. Tax liens run on another track: they attach to the parcel as of the listing date, and the remedy is a foreclosure suit filed where the land lies.

A house with liens, back taxes, tenants or repair needs can still sell for cash without a listing or showings. The deed goes to this same register and carries the same recording fee and stamp as any sale.

faqs.q: What phone number reaches the Johnston County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Dial 919-989-5160 for land records, or 919-989-5161 for vital records and marriage licenses. The office is in Suite 209 at 207 E. Johnston Street, Smithfield.

faqs.q: How much does a standard Johnston County deed cost to record?
faqs.a: The schedule shows $26.00 through page 15 with $4.00 for each page after. A deed of trust costs $64.00 through page 35. The excise stamp is billed separately at $2.00 per $1,000 of consideration.

faqs.q: Is there a charge for recording a satisfaction in Johnston County?
faqs.a: No. The schedule lists satisfactions of a security instrument, trustee's satisfactions, notices, certificates and affidavits of satisfaction at no charge.

faqs.q: Is e-recording available for Johnston County deeds?
faqs.a: Yes, through an approved submitter. CSC eRecording, EPN, Indecomm, NTC and Simplifile are listed, and your closing company normally sends the file for you.

faqs.q: Who owes the excise tax on a Johnston County sale?
faqs.a: The seller. State law has the transferor pay the register ahead of recording, at $1.00 per $500 of consideration or fraction of it.
